venues.name: Botswana Butchery

venues.name: Toast and Oak
venues.note: A wine-led kitchen doing considered, seasonal small plates, Queenstown's most food-and-wine-minded newcomer to the hats.
credentials: Cuisine Good Food Awards 2025, One Hat

venues.name: Skyline Gondola & Bob's Peak
venues.note: The steepest cable-car lift in the Southern Hemisphere climbs 480m in about ten minutes to a glass-fronted eyrie over Lake Wakatipu, with The Remarkables and Cecil and Walter Peaks laid out across the water. Ride up for a leisurely buffet at the Stratosfare Restaurant, or simply for the sundowner view, gentle enough for the grandparents, spectacular for everyone.

venues.name: The Skyline Luge
venues.note: At the top of the gondola, gravity carts wind down banked, tunnelled tracks with 220-degree views of the lake and mountains, the Blue Track a gentle cruise, the Red Track steeper and faster. It is the rare thrill that a nine-year-old and a grandfather can both take on, at their own pace, side by side.

venues.name: TSS Earnslaw Steamship Cruise to Walter Peak
venues.note: The 1912 'Lady of the Lake' is the only hand-fired coal steamship still carrying passengers in the Southern Hemisphere, a 90-minute glide across the water to Walter Peak High Country Farm, engine room open to wander and a pianist on deck. At the farm, a gourmet barbecue and a sheep-shearing show delight children while elders relax by the fire; ask for the vegetarian menu in advance.

venues.name: Queenstown Gardens & Lakefront Peninsula
venues.note: A leafy peninsula reaching into Lake Wakatipu, threaded with rose gardens, giant sequoias, a frisbee-golf course and easy flat paths right on the water, five minutes' stroll from the town centre. It is the gentle, unhurried heart of Queenstown: a picnic, a slow lakeside walk, and the mountains reflected on still mornings.

venues.name: The Queenstown Lakefront & Steamer Wharf
venues.note: The waterfront promenade is the town's living room, jetties, the historic Steamer Wharf, lakeside restaurants and the famous Fergburger queue just up the hill. Take an evening walk as the peaks turn pink, or hand the family a lakeside table for dinner with the water at your feet.

venues.name: Shotover Jet
venues.note: The only operator licensed inside the sheer Shotover Canyons, these red jet boats skim inches from rock walls at 85kph and spin the signature 360s down a river no other boat can run. A thrilling but accessible half-hour, the kind of adrenaline the teenagers demand and the parents secretly love.

venues.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy, the World's First
venues.note: AJ Hackett opened commercial bungy jumping here in 1988; the 43m leap off the historic suspension bridge into the Kawarau River is where the whole sport began. Even if no one in the family jumps, the viewing decks and cantilevered platform make it a genuine pilgrimage, watch, cheer, and photograph the leap.

venues.name: The Nevis Bungy & Swing
venues.note: Reached by 4WD across private farmland, the Nevis is New Zealand's highest bungy, a 134m plunge from a pod slung over a canyon, plus the world's biggest swing, which arcs a vast 300m and can be ridden tandem. This is the serious adventurer's badge; for the rest, the drive and the canyon setting alone are extraordinary.

venues.name: Shotover Canyon Swing & Canyon Fox
venues.note: A 60m freefall from a 109m clifftop platform before a giant 200m swing sweeps you over the river, jumped forwards, backwards or in one of dozens of theatrical release styles. It sits in the sweet spot between bungy and pure fun, with the milder Canyon Fox zipline alongside for those who prefer to watch.

venues.name: Skydive Over The Remarkables (NZONE)
venues.note: Tandem jumps from 9,000, 12,000 or 15,000 feet fall over an almost unfair panorama, the lake, the alps and the fjords all at once. It is the once-in-a-lifetime photograph; and for family members staying on the ground, the drop zone viewing is part of the theatre.

venues.name: White-Water Rafting the Shotover & Kawarau Rivers
venues.note: The Shotover delivers grade 3–5 rapids down the legendary Skippers Canyon Road and through the dark Oxenbridge Tunnel; the Kawarau runs a gentler grade 2–3 for families and first-timers. A guided, full-day wilderness outing, choose the river to match your nerve.

venues.name: Onsen Hot Pools & Day Spa
venues.area: Arthurs Point, above the Shotover River
venues.note: Private cedar-lined hot tubs perched over the Shotover gorge, where a garage-style wall slides open so you soak half-inside, half under the open alpine sky. Booked room by room, it is the discreet, restorative counterpoint to a day of adventure, a couples' soak, or the whole family unwinding with the mountains in view.

venues.name: Gibbston Valley Wine Tour
venues.note: Twenty-five minutes from town, Central Otago's 'Valley of the Vines' is world-famous for cool-climate Pinot Noir, its cellar doors strung along the Kawarau Gorge. A private-driver tour lets everyone taste freely, seated fireside at Amisfield, or deep inside the country's largest wine cave at Gibbston Valley, over a long, unhurried lunch.

venues.name: Gibbston Valley Winery, Wine Cave & Cheesery
venues.note: The region's oldest vineyard, first vintage 1987, is now a small estate in itself, a candlelit tasting in New Zealand's largest wine cave, an on-site cheesery, a bistro and a luxury lodge and spa. A single, elegant stop that satisfies serious wine lovers and casual visitors alike.

venues.name: Amisfield Cellar Door & Restaurant
venues.note: A rustic converted woolshed turned into one of the country's most acclaimed dining rooms, where the celebrated 'Trust the Kitchen' tasting menu is paired with the estate's own Pinot. Reserve well ahead; it is the definitive long lunch, and the kitchen handles vegetarian and dietary requests with real care.

venues.name: Arrowtown, Historic Gold-Rush Village
venues.note: A jewel of a settlement on the gold-bearing Arrow River, its 1860s Buckingham Street lined with more than sixty preserved miners' cottages, boutiques and cafés. A gentle, walkable day of history and browsing, with the excellent Lakes District Museum for the curious and gold-panning in the river for the children.

venues.name: Arrowtown Chinese Settlement
venues.note: At the edge of town along Bush Creek stand the restored stone huts and Ah Lum's store of the Chinese gold-miners who arrived from 1866, a quiet, moving record of a community that was pushed to the town's margins. A short, thoughtful walk that gives Arrowtown's prettiness real depth.

venues.name: Arrowtown in Autumn
venues.note: For a few weeks in April and May the town's avenues of oaks, poplars and sycamores blaze gold and amber, one of the most photographed sights in the South Island, crowned by the Arrowtown Autumn Festival. Time a visit here and the whole family walks through a painting.

venues.name: Glenorchy & Paradise
venues.area: Head of Lake Wakatipu, 45km from Queenstown
venues.note: The road to Glenorchy is itself one of the world's great drives, hugging the lake to a tiny township at the gateway of Mt Aspiring National Park and the valley literally named Paradise. Base a serene day here among braided rivers and beech forest, the setting for Lord of the Rings' Misty Mountains and Isengard.

venues.name: Dart River Wilderness Jet Safari
venues.note: A jet boat threads the braided, glacier-fed Dart through the heart of a UNESCO wilderness, with 360-degree spins and a guided walk through ancient beech forest and film locations. Faster than the TSS Earnslaw but far gentler than the Shotover, a scenic thrill that spans the generations.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Te Wāhipounamu / Mt Aspiring National Park

venues.name: High-Country Horse Riding at Glenorchy
venues.note: Guided treks cross glacial rivers and open flats beneath towering peaks, from gentle walking-pace rides for beginners to longer back-country trails. It is a soft, cinematic way into landscapes most visitors only see from a boat, well suited to a mixed-ability family group.

venues.name: Lord of the Rings 4WD Film-Location Safari (Nomad Safaris)
venues.note: A half-day 4WD tour to the real Middle-earth, the Kawarau Gorge that became the Pillars of the Kings, Deer Park Heights and The Remarkables that stood in for the Misty Mountains, with gold-panning along the way. Minimal walking and small Land Cruiser groups make it easy for every age.

venues.name: Lake Hayes Loop Walk
venues.note: A flat, beautiful 8km circuit around a mirror-still lake famous for its reflections of the surrounding hills, about two to three easy hours, or a gentle e-bike. One of the district's most relaxing outings, and a lovely stop paired with an Amisfield lunch nearby.

venues.name: Moke Lake
venues.note: A hidden, horseshoe-shaped lake ringed by hills down a short gravel road, gloriously quiet and framed for still-water reflections at dawn and dusk. A peaceful picnic, an easy loop walk or a paddle, the local's antidote to the town's bustle.

venues.name: Milford Sound Scenic Flight (Fly-Cruise-Fly)
venues.note: A 45-minute flight over the Southern Alps and glaciers to land at Milford, cruise the fjord, and fly home, often called the world's finest scenic flight, and a fraction of the driving day. The private, elevated way to see Fiordland when time and comfort matter.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Te Wāhipounamu / Fiordland National Park

venues.name: Scenic Helicopter Flight & Alpine Landing
venues.note: Shorter flights sweep over the lake, The Remarkables and Cecil and Walter Peaks with a snow or summit landing, a gentle taste of the high country for those not ready for a full heli-picnic. A superb way to give elders the alpine grandeur without a hike.

venues.name: Guided & Heli Fly-Fishing for Trout
venues.note: Gin-clear high-country rivers hold sight-fishable brown trout that can top ten pounds; a private guide walks you to spring creeks, or a helicopter drops you into pristine backcountry water no road reaches. A meditative, world-class pursuit for the angler in the family, bespoke and unhurried.

venues.name: Coronet Peak Ski Field
venues.note: The closest field to town on a fully sealed road, with wide open runs, a strong learners' area and New Zealand's only floodlit night skiing followed by après. Between roughly June and October it is the family's easy day on the snow; out of season, the summit road still rewards with sweeping views.

venues.name: The Remarkables Ski Field
venues.note: The mountain range that gives Queenstown its silhouette hides sheltered basins and one of the country's best beginner zones served by covered conveyor lifts. In winter it is a superb, uncrowded family day out; the drive up alone, in any season, is spectacular.

venues.name: Cardrona Alpine Resort
venues.note: The region's largest ski area and best all-rounder, reliably snowy, with terrain for every level and a beloved après scene, reached over the dramatic Crown Range Road, New Zealand's highest sealed pass. Worth the drive for a change of mountain, and a fine stop en route to Wanaka.

venues.name: Wanaka & the #ThatWanakaTree
venues.note: A calmer, more local-feeling lake town over the Crown Range, with a famous lone willow standing in the water, gentle waterfront walks and the quirky Puzzling World for children. An easy, pretty day trip that trades Queenstown's buzz for something more serene.

venues.name: Roys Peak Track
venues.note: New Zealand's most photographed viewpoint, a switchbacked ridge that opens onto Lake Wanaka and the Southern Alps at your feet, about a 16km, five-to-six-hour return climb. A serious but non-technical hike for the fit; start at first light to have the famous ledge to yourselves.

venues.name: The Crown Range Road & Cardrona Hotel
venues.note: New Zealand's highest sealed road switchbacks over the Crown Range with a lookout that takes in the whole Wakatipu Basin, pausing at the 1863 Cardrona Hotel, one of the country's oldest and most photogenic pubs. A scenic drive that is a destination in itself, easy for all ages with a driver.

venues.name: Skippers Canyon Scenic 4WD
venues.note: One of New Zealand's most dramatic and precipitous roads, cut by hand during the gold rush along sheer schist walls above the Shotover, driven only by licensed guides. A vertiginous, story-rich half-day of history and jaw-dropping scenery, no walking required.

venues.name: Queenstown Trail, E-Bike the Lakes & Vineyards
venues.note: A superb network of largely flat, sealed cycle trails links the lakefront, Lake Hayes, Arrowtown and the Gibbston wineries, with swing bridges over turquoise rivers along the way. On an e-bike it suits mixed fitness perfectly, pedal between cellar doors, with a support vehicle if you prefer.

venues.name: Stargazing at Bob's Peak
venues.note: From roughly March to October, expert astronomers set up high-powered telescopes at the gondola summit to tour the Milky Way and the Southern Cross under some of the clearest skies in the hemisphere. A calm, wonder-filled evening, and the Central Otago region as a whole holds Dark Sky status.

venues.name: Ziptrek Ecotours
venues.note: A guided series of ziplines and treetop platforms threads the native forest below the gondola, blending gentle thrill with a genuine conservation story and huge lake views. A crowd-pleaser that spans ages, real fun for children with an environmental lesson folded in.

venues.name: KJet, Lake & Rivers Jet Boat
venues.note: Departing right from the town pier, this hour-long ride runs Lake Wakatipu and the Kawarau and Shotover Rivers with spins and speed but a milder edge than the canyon-bound Shotover Jet. The convenient, family-friendly jet-boat option, no transfer, straight off the waterfront.

venues.name: Paragliding & Tandem Hang Gliding from Bob's Peak
venues.note: Launch off the mountain above town and soar tandem over the lake with a certified pilot, floating gently down to the lakefront, the calmest way to fly, with none of the freefall. A serene, photogenic thrill for those who want the view without the adrenaline of a skydive.

venues.name: Fergburger & the Queenstown Food Scene
venues.note: The town punches far above its size on food, from the legendary Fergburger queue to fine dining, a serious craft-beer and cocktail scene, and increasingly good Indian restaurants for a taste of home. An easy, buzzy evening out; several kitchens cater well for vegetarian and Jain preferences with notice.

venues.name: Jack's Point & Alpine Golf
venues.note: One of the world's most scenic courses runs along the lake beneath The Remarkables, its holes framed by schist tors and open water, playable by visitors and paired with a fine clubhouse. A gracious, low-key day for the golfer in the party, with the mountains for company.

venues.name: Little Blackwood
venues.note: A polished, intimate cocktail room perched over Lake Wakatipu on Steamer Wharf, the town's most decorated bar.
credentials: Best Bar in New Zealand, Hospitality New Zealand Awards for Excellence 2022

venues.name: Eichardt's Bar
venues.note: An 1867 lakefront institution, plush sofas, a roaring fire and Bollinger by the glass, inside the town's grande-dame hotel.
credentials: The bar of Eichardt's Private Hotel, a MICHELIN One-Key hotel (2025)

venues.name: Bardeaux
venues.note: A candlelit cellar bar with a great open fire, Queenstown's serious room for whisky, wine and a quiet nightcap.
credentials: A long-established Queenstown institution, one of the town's largest whisky collections
